tasks.title: Bake-off hybrid round: Opus designs, Sonnet builds
tasks.notes: From the R-013 cost discussion (2026-10-24). Data: Sonnet medium/high = pass at ~1 pt weekly plan usage (R-009 43->44%); Opus 5.5 low/medium = great (R-012 5.78M, R-013 7.57M transcript tokens, R-013 45->47% weekly). Opus output is small (R-013: 38k output vs 7.27M cache reads over 59 turns), so cost is turn count x context, not authorship. Hypothesis: Opus low writes the evidence table + build spec in few turns; Sonnet medium executes (apply, recover, capture) where turns pile up. Do: extend model-bakeoffs/PROTOCOL.md + scripts/model_bakeoff.py so a round can name a designer model and a builder model (e.g. `open --tool claude-code --model claude-sonnet-5-5-medium --designer claude-opus-5-5-low`), with the hand-off artefact (spec/script path) recorded and usage split per model; keep one apply owner (builder). Measure with task 75 units (transcript sums + plan % delta). Run >= 2 sittings before drawing conclusions (single sittings cannot separate pass from great). Cheaper still once task 76 lets the designer emit a feature_build spec instead of a custom script. Done when: the round type exists with tests and at least two hybrid sittings are scored and compared against R-009/R-012. Code+tests merged 2026-10-25 as e0e85ee (task/78-bakeoff-hybrid-designer-builder → main; 74c028b + fix 7d410b3). Round type exists (--designer/--handoff, sitting_steps_hybrid, usage by_role). Still open: run ≥2 hybrid sittings (score + usage) and compare vs R-009/R-012; wave worker could not run live Claude Code + Minecraft + interview.

tasks.title: Use pyproj for coordinate conversion instead of GDAL subprocesses
tasks.notes: User request 2026-10-25: replace GDAL for individual coordinate conversion and remove references that prescribe it for that purpose. This is explicitly NOT a blanket GDAL ban: retain appropriate uses for bulk geospatial file processing, including lidar/raster processing. Replace scripts/world_frame.py _gdal_transform/gdaltransform subprocesses with cached in-process pyproj Transformer instances, including the existing small-batch point conversion APIs. Preserve public interfaces, coordinate ordering (explicit always_xy), inverse conversions, empty-input behaviour and supported CRS handling; keep world_frame as the shared conversion boundary and geodetic.py/osgb.py as compatibility wrappers. Add pyproj to the project dependency/setup mechanism. Audit other point-conversion subprocess call sites and migrate them through the shared boundary. Update current docstrings, CLI help, setup instructions, skills and tests that describe GDAL/gdaltransform as required for point conversion (known starting points: scripts/world_frame.py, scripts/geodetic.py, scripts/geo.py, .claude/skills/new-world-build/SKILL.md); retain historical ADR context and legitimate bulk-processing references. Verify transformation accuracy against independent fixed reference coordinates, including a documented policy for OSTN15 grid availability/fallback, rather than assuming pyproj and the current GDAL installation choose identical transformations. Unit tests must use explicit fixtures and require neither an active world nor a GDAL executable. Done when: point-conversion paths run in-process through pyproj with no GDAL subprocess dependency; tests cover forward/inverse values, axis order, small batches and empty inputs; relevant current references are updated; appropriate bulk-file GDAL workflows remain supported.

tasks.title: Validate pyproj against GDAL and add fictional-world coordinate fixtures
tasks.notes: Approved plan 2026-10-25; follow-up to #84. Run a one-off GDAL comparison against the new pyproj implementation for British National Grid (EPSG:27700), WGS84 / UTM zone 18N (EPSG:32618; New York area), and NZTM2000 (EPSG:2193; Wellington area). Compare individual points and small batches in both directions. Record commands, GDAL/PROJ/pyproj versions, transformation settings, correction-grid availability (including OSTN15 where relevant), justified numerical tolerances and results in a short validation report; investigate discrepancies rather than assuming equivalent operation selection. GDAL and pyproj share PROJ, so also use published reference values where available instead of treating agreement as wholly independent proof. Do not add a permanent GDAL comparison test. Add fixed expected forward/reverse mappings among latitude/longitude, projected easting/northing and Minecraft x,z using fictional WorldFrame fixtures with explicit CRS and offsets for each grid. Cover axis order, negative Minecraft coordinates, nonzero offsets and batch conversions; assert known expected results as well as round trips. Done when: the one-off comparison is recorded and discrepancies resolved or explicitly explained; fixed fixtures for all three grids exercise the library-based tool in both directions; permanent tests require only pyproj and fixtures, never GDAL, network access, a selected real world or checkout data.

tasks.title: Add bidirectional XYZ tile positions, pixel offsets and batch conversion
tasks.notes: Approved plan 2026-10-25; depends on #84. Extend scripts/world_frame.py as the canonical coordinate interface, reusing existing XYZ/Web Mercator maths rather than adding a competing tool. Forward: accept zoom plus either latitude/longitude or Minecraft x,z; return tile code zoom/x/y plus east_px and south_px. Reverse: accept tile code and pixel offsets; return latitude/longitude or Minecraft x,z using an explicit frame or the explicitly selected active world. Agreed offset convention: floating-point pixels from the northwest corner of a 256-pixel logical tile; east increases rightward, south increases downward; offsets are not northings and do not depend on downloaded image resolution. Preserve fractional precision and existing Minecraft rounding behaviour. Extend to-wm and add from-wm with structured JSON output; provide JSON batch input from a file or stdin, reuse the single-point conversion functions and preserve input order. Latitude/longitude-only conversion must work with no selected world; Minecraft conversion requires explicit or explicitly selected world-frame configuration. Support integer zooms 0 through 30, canonical longitude [-180,180), valid Web Mercator latitudes and finite coordinates; reject malformed/out-of-range tile indices and offsets outside [0,256). Permanent tests cover known tile positions, fractional offsets, tile edges, both hemispheres, forward/reverse conversions, fictional Minecraft frames, batches, empty batches and invalid inputs; use fixed expected values and no GDAL, network or real-world checkout data. Audit existing helpers, CLIs and AI instructions for overlapping coordinate-conversion routes, including world_frame, ref_manifest, geo and provider adapters. Consolidate conversion maths into world_frame; retain necessary compatibility wrappers only as delegates. Update AI-facing documentation, skills and CLI help to teach one preferred single-point and batch interface, including offset units/directions, coordinate ordering, world selection and runnable examples. Keep tile-image fetching and evidence-sheet generation documented as distinct capabilities. Done when: both directions and batch mode work through one canonical implementation; permanent tests cover the agreed cases independently of current world; AI guidance contains no competing conversion implementations or contradictory instructions. GDAL remains allowed for appropriate bulk-file geospatial processing.

tasks.title: Include active-world contract tests in the default unit suite
tasks.notes: User-requested test refinement 2026-10-25. tests/test_active_world.py contains fixture-based contract tests but scripts/run_tests.py discovers only scripts/test_*.py. Include these contracts exactly once in the default suite, preferably by moving the module into the canonical scripts/ test location so --only can select it without a second discovery mechanism. Preserve refusal when the production active-world pointer is unset, identity/config loading and other existing contracts. Ensure tests isolate and restore environment variables, sys.modules and cached frame state so import order cannot change the rest of the suite. Tests must use temporary fictional world configuration, never a real checkout. Done when: the default runner executes the contracts, focused selection works, the suite passes with no active world selected, and no real-world dependency is introduced. Prioritised 2026-10-25 per owner: runtime improvements first. Test-refinement execution order 3/5 (#91, #90, #87, #88, #89). Third: restore missing contract coverage after the two direct runtime improvements; this closes a coverage gap rather than speeding up the suite.

tasks.title: Clean up temporary directories created by unit tests
tasks.notes: User-requested test refinement 2026-10-25. Replace unmanaged tempfile.mkdtemp() sites in scripts/test_house_build.py and scripts/test_feature_build.py (five sites identified in the review) with TemporaryDirectory contexts or test-owned TemporaryDirectory instances registered through addCleanup. Audit the remaining unit suite for equivalent unowned temporary directories. Preserve fixture lifetimes through the assertions and guarantee cleanup on failures as well as successful tests. Avoid unrelated test rewrites. Done when: all affected fixture directories have explicit cleanup ownership, affected modules pass and repeated focused runs leave no directories created by those tests behind. Prioritised 2026-10-25 per owner: runtime improvements first. Test-refinement execution order 4/5 (#91, #90, #87, #88, #89). Fourth: fix temporary-directory ownership and disk leaks; useful hygiene, with no demonstrated substantial runtime saving.

tasks.title: Prune migration-era test assertions that do not protect behaviour
tasks.notes: User-requested test refinement 2026-10-25. Review assertions against removed private methods, production source substrings and historical ticket wording. Starting examples: scripts/test_world_blockstore.py test_no_mca_reader_methods, scripts/test_model_bakeoff.py documentation wording checks, and hasattr checks in test_dryrun_reset.py/test_defra_world.py. Judge each against current accepted requirements: retain meaningful architecture/safety contracts, replace brittle implementation assertions with observable behavioural checks where useful, and delete obsolete historical assertions without replacement when no current contract remains. Do not blanket-delete documentation or negative tests. Done when: each reviewed assertion is retained with a current rationale, replaced by a meaningful behavioural check, or removed as obsolete; the change description records the decisions; affected modules and the full fixture-based suite pass. Prioritised 2026-10-25 per owner: runtime improvements first. Test-refinement execution order 5/5 (#91, #90, #87, #88, #89). Fifth: prune brittle historical assertions selectively; maintainability improvement, with little demonstrated runtime benefit. Do not remove meaningful coverage merely to reduce test count.
